response.title: which power station can keep a garage freezer cold the longest in summer heat
response.answer:
For keeping a garage freezer cold during a summer power outage, the best portable power station is one with a large battery capacity (Wh), low inverter standby consumption, and enough surge power to start the freezer compressor.

My recommendation is to look at 4–8 kWh expandable power stations rather than the smaller 1–2 kWh camping models.

The challenge is summer heat: a freezer in a 95–110°F garage may consume substantially more electricity than it does in a climate-controlled room. That can make the difference between keeping your food frozen for two days versus four days.

## Estimate your actual runtime

The following calculator uses an illustrative hot-garage freezer load and 85% usable battery capacity. Actual results depend on your freezer and the power station's idle consumption.

{@body const [daily,setDaily] = DIL.useState(1000)}
{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState("5040")}
{@body const [extra,setExtra] = DIL.useState(false)}
{@body const total = Number(capacity)*(extra?2:1)}
{@body const days = total*0.85/daily}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <box gap={1}>
    <label>Power station</label>
    <radio-group direction="col" value={capacity} onChange={setCapacity}>
      <radio value="5040">Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus — 5,040 Wh</radio>
      <radio value="4096">EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 — 4,096 Wh</radio>
      <radio value="3840">Anker SOLIX F3800 — 3,840 Wh</radio>
    </radio-group>
  </box>
  <checkbox checked={extra} onChange={setExtra} lineThrough={false}>Add one matching expansion battery</checkbox>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <label>Freezer electricity use</label>
    **{daily.toLocaleString("en-US")} Wh/day**
  </row>
  <slider min={500} max={2000} step={100} value={daily} onChange={setDaily}/>
  <row justify="between">
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Efficient freezer</text>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Hot garage / high consumption</text>
  </row>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} align="center" gap={1}>
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Estimated continuous backup runtime</text>
    <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{days.toFixed(1)} days</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">{(days*24).toFixed(0)} hours · {total.toLocaleString("en-US")} Wh nominal capacity</text>
  </box>
</box>

One important consideration: the Jackery 5000 Plus has a specified maximum discharge ambient temperature of 113°F. I would keep the battery in a cooler, ventilated indoor location and run a suitably rated cable to the freezer rather than expose it to extreme garage heat. <Cite ref="turn489047search12"/>

## One question that would change my recommendation

**Is your garage freezer a chest freezer or an upright freezer, and roughly how many cubic feet is it?**

With that information, I can narrow down which power station will actually keep it frozen the longest without spending unnecessarily on a huge battery.
